output.title: Decreasing students’ stress through time management training

scenes.narration: University students often feel stressed, and this paper asks whether a short time management training can change that in higher education.
scenes.layout_description: A student sits at a desk surrounded by papers, with a small clock and an orange arrow pointing toward a calmer posture.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal hand-drawn student at cluttered desk, clock nearby, stress lines around head, orange arrow toward a calmer face, cream background, black ink line art with orange and yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: The authors studied twenty-three undergraduate students who attended one training and reported demands, perceived stress, and perceived control of time before and after.
scenes.layout_description: Three simple labeled boxes sit beside a student figure, showing the same person at three moments in a timeline.
scenes.visual_prompt: A single student repeated in three small panels along a line, with icons for demands, tension, and control, minimalist black ink with orange highlights.

scenes.narration: They used a non-equivalent dependent variable design, meaning demands should stay unchanged while stress and control of time should shift after training.
scenes.layout_description: A balance-like sketch shows two expected-changing scales and one steady scale in the middle.
scenes.visual_prompt: Three hanging scales: one labeled stress, one control, one demands; middle demands scale stays level while the others tilt, orange circles marking change.

scenes.narration: The training was meant to help students prioritize, set goals, plan daily work, monitor progress, and use time management strategies.
scenes.layout_description: A sequence of small icons shows a checklist, a target, a calendar, and a checkmark flowing left to right.
scenes.visual_prompt: Four simple hand-drawn icons in a row: checklist, target, calendar, checkmark, connected by orange arrows on cream background.

scenes.narration: Participants reflected on their activities, chose important ones, set concrete goals, planned steps, and thought about obstacles and deadlines.
scenes.layout_description: A student stands beside sticky-note-like shapes arranged around a goal flag and a small obstacle rock.
scenes.visual_prompt: Student thinking with speech bubble shapes, goal flag ahead, stepping stones and a small rock obstacle, orange highlights on the flag and deadlines.

scenes.narration: They also planned their work day and monitored task completion, aiming to make studies more organized and less stressful.
scenes.layout_description: A simple calendar page fills the center, with tasks checked off and a small stress cloud shrinking nearby.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn calendar with checkmarks, tiny clock, and a cloud fading with an orange arrow, minimalist and spacious.

scenes.narration: The sample came from a medium-sized German university, with students from all faculties invited through boards, newsletters, and seminars.
scenes.layout_description: A campus notice board and newsletter sheet sit beside a small university building outline.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple university building, notice board, and paper newsletter icons, with students approaching, black ink and orange accents.

scenes.narration: The training lasted four hours, and questionnaires were completed before training, then two weeks later, and again four weeks later.
scenes.layout_description: A horizontal timeline shows three survey points spaced across the slide with a clock above the first point.
scenes.visual_prompt: Timeline with three dots and paper forms at each point, a small clock over the first dot, orange arrows marking the follow-up points.

scenes.narration: Of the forty-eight students who began, twenty-three completed all questionnaires and formed the main analysis sample.
scenes.layout_description: A funnel-like drawing narrows from many figures to a smaller group of twenty-three.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple group of student icons narrowing into a smaller cluster of 23, with papers beside them, cream background and orange funnel arrow.

scenes.narration: Those twenty-three students averaged 23.30 years old, and 52 percent were female; they studied several different subjects.
scenes.layout_description: A central student figure is surrounded by small subject symbols and a gender split marker.
scenes.visual_prompt: One student icon with surrounding tiny symbols for different subjects, a small pie-like split marked 52 percent, orange and yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: Before training, most students reported no or little experience with time management strategies, which the authors thought might matter.
scenes.layout_description: Two nearly empty experience bars sit beside a student looking uncertain at a clock.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal bar-like experience scale with low fills, student and clock, orange emphasis on the low bars.

scenes.narration: The researchers measured time management behaviour, perceived stress using the tension scale, perceived control of time, and demands.
scenes.layout_description: Four labeled circles cluster around a central student, each circle representing one study variable.
scenes.visual_prompt: Central student with four surrounding circles for behavior, tension, control, and demands, black ink with orange and yellow markers.

scenes.narration: At time one, time management behaviour correlated positively with perceived control of time, while stress and demands were strongly related.
scenes.layout_description: A simple correlation web connects the four variables with thicker lines between stress and demands.
scenes.visual_prompt: Network of circles and connecting lines, thicker orange line between stress and demands, smaller line between behavior and control.

scenes.narration: After training, reported use of the taught strategies increased significantly by four weeks, and the two-week increase was nearly significant.
scenes.layout_description: A rising line climbs from the first to third measurement point, with a smaller rise at the second point.
scenes.visual_prompt: Upward line graph with three points, orange arrow rising more clearly by the third point, minimalist and hand-drawn.

scenes.narration: For perceived stress, the repeated-measures analysis showed a significant overall time effect and a significant decrease after two weeks.
scenes.layout_description: A before-and-after pair of tension clouds sits above a small results table icon.
scenes.visual_prompt: Two clouds, the second smaller and lower, with an orange downward arrow between them and a tiny stats symbol.

scenes.narration: Perceived control of time showed only a tendency after two weeks, but by four weeks it had increased significantly.
scenes.layout_description: A clock icon grows steadier across two follow-up points, with the later point highlighted in orange.
scenes.visual_prompt: Clock face becoming more centered and stable across three small frames, orange highlight on the final frame showing stronger control.

scenes.narration: At four weeks, students reported less perceived stress and more perceived control of time than before training.
scenes.layout_description: Two arrows point in opposite directions from the pretest to the final follow-up, one down for stress and one up for control.
scenes.visual_prompt: Split scene with a stress cloud moving down and a clock moving up, both linked to the final time point.

scenes.narration: The control variable, demands, did not change significantly at either follow-up, which matched the study design.
scenes.layout_description: A steady horizontal line labeled demands stays flat across the three measurement points.
scenes.visual_prompt: Flat line with three dots for demands across time, no rise or fall, orange circle around the unchanged line.

scenes.narration: The authors say the pattern supports the conclusion that training reduced stress and increased perceived control of time.
scenes.layout_description: A summary arrow points from the training scene toward two outcome icons, stress and control.
scenes.visual_prompt: Training icon in the center with two outcome arrows: one to a smaller stress cloud, one to a stronger clock, orange and yellow emphasis.

scenes.narration: They also note the effects seemed stronger for students with no or little prior experience than for those with more experience.
scenes.layout_description: Two side-by-side student groups are shown, with the less-experienced group highlighted more brightly.
scenes.visual_prompt: Two small student clusters, one with larger orange arrows showing bigger change, the other with smaller arrows, minimalist comparison.

scenes.narration: The authors suggest prioritizing, goal setting, daily planning, and monitoring may give students more orientation and reduce stress.
scenes.layout_description: A student follows a path marked by a target, calendar, and checklist, with a clearer route than before.
scenes.visual_prompt: Path or stepping stones leading to a goal flag, with calendar and checklist icons guiding the way, orange arrows showing direction.

scenes.narration: They also argue that monitoring can show completed tasks, creating reinforcing information that may help stress.
scenes.layout_description: A checklist fills with checkmarks, and a small positive spark appears beside it.
scenes.visual_prompt: Checklist with several checked boxes, tiny spark or star beside it, black ink with yellow spark and orange checkmarks.

scenes.narration: The study has limits: the sample was small, and about half the students left before the second measurement.
scenes.layout_description: A small group of students fades into a smaller group across a timeline, emphasizing dropout.
scenes.visual_prompt: Group of students shrinking along a timeline, with some figures fading out, orange arrow showing attrition.

scenes.narration: The authors say larger student samples and more intervention studies are needed before stronger conclusions can be drawn.
scenes.layout_description: A magnifying glass hovers over a larger crowd of student icons, suggesting future research.
scenes.visual_prompt: Magnifying glass over many student figures and paper sheets, orange highlight around the larger sample idea.

scenes.narration: They also suggest comparing time management training with other stress-reducing interventions to learn how effective it really is.
scenes.layout_description: Two different intervention paths branch from one starting point, inviting comparison.
scenes.visual_prompt: Forked path with one route labeled time management and another generic stress intervention icon, orange arrows on both paths.

scenes.narration: For practice, they recommend teaching students to prioritize, set clear goals, plan work days, and monitor progress.
scenes.layout_description: A compact toolkit of four study habits sits in a neat row like tools on a table.
scenes.visual_prompt: Four tool-like icons—priority list, target, calendar, checklist—arranged neatly, orange and yellow highlights on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Overall, this paper suggests a short training may help students feel less stressed and more in control of time.
scenes.layout_description: A final calm student stands beside a steady clock and a smaller stress cloud, closing the slideshow.
scenes.visual_prompt: Peaceful student with upright posture beside a clock and tiny fading stress cloud, orange halo around the clock, minimalist closing scene.
